ar.pk_results_intro: What the simulation means for {{name}} — in simple terms.
ar.pk_res_peak_explain: The maximum active substance level you reach with this dose — normalized to 100 %. All other values are shown relative to it.
ar.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
ar.pk_res_half_explain: After {{h}} hours, half of the substance has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h it is practically completely eliminated. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
ar.pk_res_duration_explain: Once the level drops below 10 %, the effect is negligible. This gives you a rough idea of how long a dose is actually active.
ar.pk_res_f_explain: {{pct}} % of the injected amount actually reaches the bloodstream. The rest is broken down before it takes effect. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
ar.pk_res_vd_high: High value (> 1 L/kg) — the substance is stored heavily in tissue, not just in the blood. This often explains a longer duration of effect.
ar.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
ar.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.
ar.pk_res_accum_strong: That is strong accumulation — the substance builds up considerably.

es.pk_res_peak_explain: The maximum active substance level you reach with this dose — normalized to 100 %. All other values are shown relative to it.
es.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
es.pk_res_half_explain: After {{h}} hours, half of the substance has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h it is practically completely eliminated. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
es.pk_res_duration_explain: Once the level drops below 10 %, the effect is negligible. This gives you a rough idea of how long a dose is actually active.
es.pk_res_f_explain: {{pct}} % of the injected amount actually reaches the bloodstream. The rest is broken down before it takes effect. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
es.pk_res_vd_high: High value (> 1 L/kg) — the substance is stored heavily in tissue, not just in the blood. This often explains a longer duration of effect.
es.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
es.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.
es.pk_res_accum_strong: That is strong accumulation — the substance builds up considerably.

fr.my_stack_strength_hint_reconstituted: Un flacon de poudre (peptide) se dissout avant la première prise — la reconstitution. À gauche, la quantité de principe actif dans le flacon ; à droite, la quantité de solvant que tu ajoutes. Exemple : 10 mg dans 2 ml donnent 5 mg/ml. Si le flacon est déjà liquide, les deux chiffres figurent sur l’étiquette. Pas une recommandation de dosage.
fr.my_stack_strength_hint_per_mass: Quelle quantité de principe actif contient une quantité de produit ? Saisis ce qui figure sur l’emballage. Exemple : 50 mg pour 1 g. Pas une recommandation de dosage.

fr.pk_stat_peak_sub: When the most active substance is in the blood after the last injection.
fr.pk_stat_half_life_sub: After {{h}} h, half has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h the substance is practically gone. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
fr.pk_stat_tmax_sub: After the injection it takes about {{h}} h for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
fr.pk_stat_bioavailability_sub: {{pct}} % of the injected amount reaches the bloodstream. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
fr.pk_stat_vd_sub: Indicates how widely the substance spreads into body tissue.
fr.pk_stat_vd_high: High value — it is stored heavily in tissue, which often explains a longer duration of effect.
fr.pk_stat_vd_low: Low value — it stays mainly in the blood.
fr.pk_stat_ke_sub: Each hour, {{pct}} % of the remaining substance is cleared. Small value = slow clearance = long duration of effect.

fr.pk_manual_intro: Simulate the theoretical course of a single dose — choose substance, dose and route. The values are estimates based on average pharmacological data.

fr.pk_field_dose_tip: The amount you inject. Tip: check your active cycle for your usual dose.
fr.pk_field_unit_tip: mcg = micrograms (smaller), mg = milligrams (larger), IU = international units (for HGH/HCG)
fr.pk_field_route_tip: SC = subcutaneous (under the skin, slower), IM = intramuscular (into the muscle, somewhat faster)
fr.pk_curve_sub: Relative active substance level in % (normalized to peak = 100 %)
fr.pk_results_intro: What the simulation means for {{name}} — in simple terms.
fr.pk_res_peak_explain: The maximum active substance level you reach with this dose — normalized to 100 %. All other values are shown relative to it.
fr.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
fr.pk_res_half_explain: After {{h}} hours, half of the substance has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h it is practically completely eliminated. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
fr.pk_res_duration_explain: Once the level drops below 10 %, the effect is negligible. This gives you a rough idea of how long a dose is actually active.
fr.pk_res_f_explain: {{pct}} % of the injected amount actually reaches the bloodstream. The rest is broken down before it takes effect. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
fr.pk_res_vd_high: High value (> 1 L/kg) — the substance is stored heavily in tissue, not just in the blood. This often explains a longer duration of effect.
fr.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
fr.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.
fr.pk_res_accum_strong: That is strong accumulation — the substance builds up considerably.

hi.pk_stat_peak_sub: When the most active substance is in the blood after the last injection.

hi.pk_results_intro: What the simulation means for {{name}} — in simple terms.
hi.pk_res_peak_explain: The maximum active substance level you reach with this dose — normalized to 100 %. All other values are shown relative to it.
hi.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
hi.pk_res_half_explain: After {{h}} hours, half of the substance has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h it is practically completely eliminated. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
hi.pk_res_duration_explain: Once the level drops below 10 %, the effect is negligible. This gives you a rough idea of how long a dose is actually active.
hi.pk_res_f_explain: {{pct}} % of the injected amount actually reaches the bloodstream. The rest is broken down before it takes effect. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
hi.pk_res_vd_high: High value (> 1 L/kg) — the substance is stored heavily in tissue, not just in the blood. This often explains a longer duration of effect.
hi.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
hi.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.
hi.pk_res_accum_strong: That is strong accumulation — the substance builds up considerably.

id.pk_results_intro: What the simulation means for {{name}} — in simple terms.
id.pk_res_peak_explain: The maximum active substance level you reach with this dose — normalized to 100 %. All other values are shown relative to it.
id.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
id.pk_res_half_explain: After {{h}} hours, half of the substance has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h it is practically completely eliminated. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
id.pk_res_duration_explain: Once the level drops below 10 %, the effect is negligible. This gives you a rough idea of how long a dose is actually active.
id.pk_res_f_explain: {{pct}} % of the injected amount actually reaches the bloodstream. The rest is broken down before it takes effect. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
id.pk_res_vd_high: High value (> 1 L/kg) — the substance is stored heavily in tissue, not just in the blood. This often explains a longer duration of effect.
id.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
id.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.
id.pk_res_accum_strong: That is strong accumulation — the substance builds up considerably.

it.my_stack_strength_hint_per_unit: Quanto principio attivo contiene UNA unità? Inserisci il valore riportato sulla confezione. Esempio: 500 mg per 1 capsula. La quantità di prodotto è già impostata su 1: cambiala solo se la confezione indica diversamente. Non è una raccomandazione di dosaggio.

it.my_stack_strength_hint_reconstituted: Un flaconcino di polvere (peptide) viene sciolto prima della prima assunzione: la ricostituzione. A sinistra quanto principio attivo c’è nel flaconcino, a destra quanto solvente aggiungi. Esempio: 10 mg in 2 ml danno 5 mg/ml. Se il flaconcino è già liquido, entrambi i valori sono sull’etichetta. Non è una raccomandazione di dosaggio.

ja.pk_stat_peak_sub: When the most active substance is in the blood after the last injection.
ja.pk_stat_half_life_sub: After {{h}} h, half has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h the substance is practically gone. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
ja.pk_stat_tmax_sub: After the injection it takes about {{h}} h for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
ja.pk_stat_bioavailability_sub: {{pct}} % of the injected amount reaches the bloodstream. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
ja.pk_stat_vd_sub: Indicates how widely the substance spreads into body tissue.
ja.pk_stat_vd_high: High value — it is stored heavily in tissue, which often explains a longer duration of effect.
ja.pk_stat_vd_low: Low value — it stays mainly in the blood.
ja.pk_stat_ke_sub: Each hour, {{pct}} % of the remaining substance is cleared. Small value = slow clearance = long duration of effect.

ja.pk_curve_sub: Relative active substance level in % (normalized to peak = 100 %)
ja.pk_results_intro: What the simulation means for {{name}} — in simple terms.
ja.pk_res_peak_explain: The maximum active substance level you reach with this dose — normalized to 100 %. All other values are shown relative to it.
ja.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
ja.pk_res_half_explain: After {{h}} hours, half of the substance has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h it is practically completely eliminated. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
ja.pk_res_duration_explain: Once the level drops below 10 %, the effect is negligible. This gives you a rough idea of how long a dose is actually active.
ja.pk_res_f_explain: {{pct}} % of the injected amount actually reaches the bloodstream. The rest is broken down before it takes effect. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
ja.pk_res_vd_high: High value (> 1 L/kg) — the substance is stored heavily in tissue, not just in the blood. This often explains a longer duration of effect.
ja.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
ja.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.
ja.pk_res_accum_strong: That is strong accumulation — the substance builds up considerably.

ko.pk_curve_sub: Relative active substance level in % (normalized to peak = 100 %)
ko.pk_results_intro: What the simulation means for {{name}} — in simple terms.
ko.pk_res_peak_explain: The maximum active substance level you reach with this dose — normalized to 100 %. All other values are shown relative to it.
ko.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
ko.pk_res_half_explain: After {{h}} hours, half of the substance has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h it is practically completely eliminated. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
ko.pk_res_duration_explain: Once the level drops below 10 %, the effect is negligible. This gives you a rough idea of how long a dose is actually active.
ko.pk_res_f_explain: {{pct}} % of the injected amount actually reaches the bloodstream. The rest is broken down before it takes effect. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
ko.pk_res_vd_high: High value (> 1 L/kg) — the substance is stored heavily in tissue, not just in the blood. This often explains a longer duration of effect.
ko.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
ko.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.
ko.pk_res_accum_strong: That is strong accumulation — the substance builds up considerably.

pt.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.

pt.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
pt.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.

ru.pk_results_intro: What the simulation means for {{name}} — in simple terms.
ru.pk_res_peak_explain: The maximum active substance level you reach with this dose — normalized to 100 %. All other values are shown relative to it.
ru.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
ru.pk_res_half_explain: After {{h}} hours, half of the substance has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h it is practically completely eliminated. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
ru.pk_res_duration_explain: Once the level drops below 10 %, the effect is negligible. This gives you a rough idea of how long a dose is actually active.
ru.pk_res_f_explain: {{pct}} % of the injected amount actually reaches the bloodstream. The rest is broken down before it takes effect. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
ru.pk_res_vd_high: High value (> 1 L/kg) — the substance is stored heavily in tissue, not just in the blood. This often explains a longer duration of effect.
ru.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
ru.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.
ru.pk_res_accum_strong: That is strong accumulation — the substance builds up considerably.

tr.pk_stat_peak_sub: When the most active substance is in the blood after the last injection.

tr.pk_results_intro: What the simulation means for {{name}} — in simple terms.
tr.pk_res_peak_explain: The maximum active substance level you reach with this dose — normalized to 100 %. All other values are shown relative to it.
tr.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
tr.pk_res_half_explain: After {{h}} hours, half of the substance has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h it is practically completely eliminated. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
tr.pk_res_duration_explain: Once the level drops below 10 %, the effect is negligible. This gives you a rough idea of how long a dose is actually active.
tr.pk_res_f_explain: {{pct}} % of the injected amount actually reaches the bloodstream. The rest is broken down before it takes effect. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
tr.pk_res_vd_high: High value (> 1 L/kg) — the substance is stored heavily in tissue, not just in the blood. This often explains a longer duration of effect.
tr.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
tr.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.
tr.pk_res_accum_strong: That is strong accumulation — the substance builds up considerably.

zh.pk_stat_peak_sub: When the most active substance is in the blood after the last injection.
zh.pk_stat_half_life_sub: After {{h}} h, half has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h the substance is practically gone. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
zh.pk_stat_tmax_sub: After the injection it takes about {{h}} h for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
zh.pk_stat_bioavailability_sub: {{pct}} % of the injected amount reaches the bloodstream. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
zh.pk_stat_vd_sub: Indicates how widely the substance spreads into body tissue.
zh.pk_stat_vd_high: High value — it is stored heavily in tissue, which often explains a longer duration of effect.
zh.pk_stat_vd_low: Low value — it stays mainly in the blood.
zh.pk_stat_ke_sub: Each hour, {{pct}} % of the remaining substance is cleared. Small value = slow clearance = long duration of effect.
zh.pk_sim_subtitle: See at a glance when your peptide takes effect and when it has been cleared again
zh.pk_sim_disclaimer: All values are based on pharmacological models and are estimates — not medical advice.
zh.pk_history_hint: 7-day window with real intakes · swipe to scroll
zh.pk_manual_intro: Simulate the theoretical course of a single dose — choose substance, dose and route. The values are estimates based on average pharmacological data.
zh.pk_field_substance_tip: Choose the substance you want to simulate. The pharmacokinetic data (half-life, Tmax) is loaded automatically.
zh.pk_no_profiles: No PK profiles yet. Add them in the admin panel.
zh.pk_field_dose_tip: The amount you inject. Tip: check your active cycle for your usual dose.
zh.pk_field_unit_tip: mcg = micrograms (smaller), mg = milligrams (larger), IU = international units (for HGH/HCG)
zh.pk_field_route_tip: SC = subcutaneous (under the skin, slower), IM = intramuscular (into the muscle, somewhat faster)
zh.pk_curve_sub: Relative active substance level in % (normalized to peak = 100 %)
zh.pk_results_intro: What the simulation means for {{name}} — in simple terms.
zh.pk_res_peak_explain: The maximum active substance level you reach with this dose — normalized to 100 %. All other values are shown relative to it.
zh.pk_res_tmax_explain: After the injection it takes about {{h}} hours for the substance to reach its highest level in the blood. Only from this point are you at maximum effect.
zh.pk_res_half_explain: After {{h}} hours, half of the substance has been cleared. After {{h2}} h it is 75 %, and after {{h5}} h it is practically completely eliminated. The longer the half-life, the less often you need to dose.
zh.pk_res_duration_explain: Once the level drops below 10 %, the effect is negligible. This gives you a rough idea of how long a dose is actually active.
zh.pk_res_f_explain: {{pct}} % of the injected amount actually reaches the bloodstream. The rest is broken down before it takes effect. For subcutaneous injection (SC) this value is typically high.
zh.pk_res_vd_high: High value (> 1 L/kg) — the substance is stored heavily in tissue, not just in the blood. This often explains a longer duration of effect.
zh.pk_res_vd_low: Low value — the substance stays mainly in the blood.
zh.pk_res_accum_explain: With regular dosing at your chosen interval, the steady-state level is {{f}} times as high as after the first dose.
zh.pk_res_accum_strong: That is strong accumulation — the substance builds up considerably.
